equity_bridge.note: Y444,103m book at 2026-06-30 less ~Y38bn deferred tax on embedded gains; income from these assets (dividends, equity-method) is excluded from the flows
2026-06-30 balance sheet; Toyo is 100%-owned so this is legacy minorities

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2027 guidance +15.8% incl. full-year Toyo consolidation, then 1-3%/yr in line with nominal Japanese construction investment)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.4-4.6%) diverges >30% from EPS CAGR (18-62%): EPS is measured from the FY2021/FY2023 cost-inflation trough into the FY2026 margin peak, and the share count fell 22% over five years (209m -> 163m) through buybacks funded partly by cross-holding sales. Neither is a repeatable growth rate; the equity CAGR is depressed by Y230bn of buybacks and Y150bn of dividends over the period.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex) less interest income; SBC is zero throughout. FCF CAGRs are not meaningful for a contractor: owner FCF was 54.3bn (FY2021), 66.4bn, 13.4bn, -83.0bn (FY2024, Y122bn capex year), -47.2bn (FY2025, Y74bn receivables build), 68.1bn (FY2026). Revenue CAGRs are flattered by FY2024-26 cost pass-through and by six months of Toyo in FY2026; the FY2002-FY2026 revenue CAGR is ~0.9%.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance year then mid-cycle. FY2027 follows management (Y2,420bn sales, Y188bn operating income); orders guided at Y2.33tn are below sales, so growth fades to 1-3% and the margin glides from the FY2026 repricing peak (EBITDA 9.8%) to 7.5% by FY2032. The Toyo acquisition adds scale and marine capability but was debt-funded; its leverage sits in net debt rather than the flows. Buybacks are value-neutral; cross-holdings (~Y405bn after tax) are added in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: Pricing discipline holds. The Big-5 oligopoly plus a 30%-smaller skilled workforce keep contract margins near FY2026 levels (EBITDA ~9% fading only to 8.5%); data-centre and fab construction, Tokyo/Osaka redevelopment and Toyo's offshore-wind pipeline keep sales growing 2-5% beyond the guidance year; continued cross-holding sales fund buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bear: Peak-cycle margins. The FY2025-26 repricing windfall proves transient: input-cost re-acceleration and wage inflation compress margins faster than the backlog reprices, orders keep falling after the Q1 FY2027 -24.5%, sales contract in FY2028-29 and margins revert to the two-decade average; Toyo integration disappoints while the acquisition debt stays. FCF stays positive, so this is a de-rating case, not a solvency case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A Japanese general contractor is valued on normalised, not peak, cash margins. FY2026 operating income of Y188bn (9.0%) is the best since FY2018 and sits on top of a 2.2% trough two years earlier; management's own FY2027 guide (7.8%) already concedes some fade. The DCF therefore anchors year 1 on guidance, fades margins to a stated mid-cycle level per scenario, charges working capital against growth, treats SBC as zero (visible), carries the Toyo acquisition debt in net debt, adds the Y405bn cross-shareholding book once (its income is excluded from the flows), deducts NCI once, and caps the terminal value at 12x FCF so Gordon cannot assume a multiple the market has never paid a contractor.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly Y1,200-1,500/share; the base 7.5% is above the 20-year average and below the last ten years' average
Working-capital seasonality and lumpiness: owner FCF swung from +68bn to -83bn over FY2024-26; the -10% capture is an average, and any single year can deviate by Y100bn
Cross-shareholding value (~Y2,500/share) depends on equity-market levels and on management continuing to monetise rather than hoard
Toyo Construction integration, goodwill (Y73.6bn) impairment risk and the higher interest bill as BOJ normalises; non-recourse SPC debt is included in net debt
Capex intensity: real-estate-for-lease development can run well above the 1.8-2.5% modelled (FY2024: 6.9% of sales)
Order intake already falling; a sharper domestic private-capex downturn than the bear path would push value toward the bear case

inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market: only a director Board Benefit Trust (BBT-RS); provision Y371m at 2026-03-31 (FY2026 tanshin BS line 577). No cash-flow SBC add-back line exists; recorded explicitly as 0.
inputs.share_count_basis: 163,185,872 issued less 177,251 treasury (incl. 98,400 BBT trust shares) at 2026-06-30 = 163,008,621 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin). No dilutive securities (diluted EPS reported as '-'). Held FLAT: buybacks (Y78.0bn FY2026, Y82.1bn FY2025) are value-neutral in this model and are funded; they are not projected as accretion.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY build, identical across scenarios (risk lives in the scenario flows, not the rate). Normalised JGB 10y ~2.5% (spot ~1.7% but a decade of suppression), ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.0 for a domestic cyclical contractor -> cost of equity ~8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~1.5% (bank loans + bonds, after-tax ~1.0%); D/(D+E) at market ~20% (Y450bn debt vs Y1.85tn market cap) -> WACC ~6.6%, rounded up to 7.0%. Below the house ~9% reference for small keiretsu suppliers because Taisei is a Y1.85tn large-cap with one-third public-sector revenue.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt. J-GAAP filer: operating leases are already expensed in cost of sales/SG&A; only finance-lease liabilities exist (Y714m current + Y1,863m non-current = Y2,577m at 2026-03-31, FY2026 tanshin BS lines 559/573) and are added to total_debt. No lease principal is deducted from the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; non-controlling interests of Y41,723m (2026-06-30) deducted once in the equity bridge. Toyo Construction is 100%-owned after the Sept-2025 TOB + share consolidation + Toyo self-tender from Maeda, so the remaining NCI is legacy minorities in smaller subsidiaries (NCI profit Y4.8bn in FY2026).
inputs.net_debt_note: 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin): cash and deposits 207,325 + marketable securities 35,000 = 242,325. Interest-bearing debt: short-term loans 138,866 + non-recourse ST 15 + bonds due <1y 10,000 + bonds 40,000 + non-recourse bonds 300 + long-term loans 208,914 + non-recourse LT loans 48,934 = 447,029; plus finance leases 2,577 (Mar-26) = 449,606. Non-recourse debt (~Y49bn, real-estate SPCs) kept in debt. June is seasonally cash-light for Japanese contractors (March collections paid out in Q1): net debt was ~Y190bn at 2026-03-31 vs ~Y207bn at 2026-06-30; the later, less favourable figure is used.
inputs.equity_bridge_note: Matching-asset rule: interest income (Y1,577m), dividend income (Y5,634m) and equity-method income (Y5,729m) are all outside operating income and therefore outside the EBITDA-driven flows, so their source assets enter the bridge: investment securities Y444,103m at 2026-06-30 (of which available-for-sale listed equities ~Y225bn at fair value with ~Y151bn embedded gains at 2026-03-31, yuho securities note line 6843; the rest is equity-method affiliates and unlisted shares at book). Deducted ~Y38bn of deferred tax on the unrealised AFS gains (30.6% x ~Y123bn gain implied by the Y85.9bn net-of-tax reserve at June-26) -> Y405,000m added. Pension surplus (Y94bn net asset) NOT added. Cross-holdings are being actively monetised (Y90bn sold in FY2026, Y115bn in FY2025) and fund the buybacks.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'; adaptations file read: JPY WACC, J-GAAP leases, NCI once, matching-asset bridge, SBC-zero, risk charged once). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. EBITDA is defined as operating income + depreciation (DB convention, FY2026 = 187,973 + 16,766 = 204,739, 9.8% of sales); goodwill amortisation (Y5.8bn in FY2026 for six months of Toyo, ~Y10bn/yr forward) is treated as a cost inside the margin, matching how management guides operating income. The unlevered flows ignore the interest-cost rise management cites for the FY2027 net-income decline; that cost is carried in the Y207bn net debt instead. PEAK-MARGIN GUARD: FY2026's 9.0% operating margin is the best since FY2018 (11.5%) after a 2.2% trough in FY2024; management itself guides FY2027 operating margin down to 7.8% (Y188bn on Y2,420bn) and orders down to Y2.33tn (below sales, so backlog starts shrinking). The base case follows guidance in year 1 and fades the EBITDA margin to a 7.5% mid-cycle level (operating ~6.5%), roughly the FY2017-FY2026 average of ~7.9% EBITDA less a haircut; the bear fades to the 20-year average (~5.5% EBITDA). Working capital: receivables + CIP + real-estate inventory exceed payables + customer advances + deposits by ~Y270bn (~13% of sales), so growth consumes cash: wc_capture -10%. Capex is lumpy (Y12-16bn/yr in FY2020-23, Y122bn FY2024, Y32bn FY2025, Y78bn FY2026 incl. real-estate-for-lease and Toyo); modelled at 2.5% of sales for two years (TAISEI VISION 2030 growth investment) tapering to 1.8% (~10-yr average 2.0%). Price is an intraday Tokyo print and should be refreshed at the regular close.

bear.narrative: FY2027 sales land near guidance (backlog + Toyo are mechanical) but margins miss as Middle-East-driven material/energy inflation and wage inflation outrun contract repricing; the -24.5% Q1 order drop proves to be the top of the large-building cycle, sales fall 3%/2% in FY2028-29 and the EBITDA margin reverts to the 20-year average (~5.5%, operating ~4.5%); terminal growth 0.5%.

base.narrative: Year 1 is management's FY2027 guidance (sales Y2,420bn, operating income Y188bn = 7.8%, EBITDA ~8.7% with ~Y22bn D&A incl. Toyo). Growth then drops to 1-3% as orders (guided Y2.33tn) fall below sales and backlog shrinks; the EBITDA margin fades from the FY2026 peak to a 7.5% mid-cycle level by year 6. Capex 2.5% -> 1.8%, WC consumes 10% of incremental sales, cash tax 30%. Terminal: 1.0% growth, cap 12x FCF (cyclical).

bull.narrative: FY2027 beats guidance as it did through FY2026; Big-5 pricing discipline under a structural labour shortage holds EBITDA at ~9% (operating ~8%) and only drifts to 8.5%; data-centre/semiconductor-fab, Tokyo redevelopment and Toyo's offshore-wind/port work sustain 2-5% growth; terminal growth 1.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear raised because the valuation hinges on how much of the FY2026 margin peak persists and order intake has already turned (-24.5% YoY in Q1 FY2027, FY2027 orders guided below sales); bull cut because it needs pricing discipline, the fab/data-centre cycle and Toyo integration all to hold at once. No solvency risk (net debt/EBITDA ~1x), so bear is not pushed higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
